div.head: Wif 9
div.ab: Wel is eac to warnianne, ðæt man wite, ðæt hy ðurh mægsibbe to gelænge ne beon, ðe læs ðe man eft twæme, ðæt man ær awoh tosomne gedydan.
Wel is eac to werianne, þæt man wite, þæt hy ðurh mæigsibbe to gelænge ne beon, ðe læs ðe man eft twæme, þæt mæn ær awoh tosomne gedydon.
Bonum est etiam pręuidere, ut non ex aliqua consanguinitate sibi pertineant, ne iuste postmodum separentur, qui sceleratis nuptiis conuenerunt.

Auch ist wohl Acht zu geben (vorzubeugen B), dass man sich vorsehe, dass die [Brautleute] nicht durch Verwandtschaft zu nahe angehörig seien, damit man nicht nachher trennen müsse, was man vorher rechtswidrig zusammengethan hatte.

It is also well to take heed (to guard against it, B) that one makes sure that [the couple] are not too closely related by kinship, lest one must afterwards separate what had previously been wrongly joined together.
It is also well to take care that one knows that they are not too closely related, lest one afterwards put asunder what was previously wrongly joined together.
div.note: H has ‘man’ with a plural verb (compare I Cn 15.1, 24, II Cn 3, 60 MS B). In B, Wer follows, as in the Quadripartitus; in H a charm against cattle theft, then Becwæð.
